boat.construction_details: She is American yellow pine (this has been confirmed by laboratory analysis) on oak frames (1 1/4" x 7/8" on 8" centres), and of traditional carvel construction, using copper fastenings. She is 3/4 decked, and the deck planking is sheathed with e-glass. External underwater areas are sheathed with Kevlar using resorcinol adhesive.

for_sales.sales_text: Log 83/4 21 ft. centreboard three-quarter decked sloop. Believed to have been built in the 1880s by Inmans yard (now Berthon boatyard) at Lymington. The boat has wintered in the same shed, which was built for her (and her sisters) since 1913 at Christchurch till for sale in '83. Professionally maintained all her life. Performance remarkable. In 3 OGA' races she has 2 firsts & a second.

boat.full_description:
Ianthe is a 24ft 6in gaff sloop with topsail, built in 1898 by Camper & Nicholsons and designed by Percival Hart, a Christchurch‑born naval architect whose early career included work for Berthon and Camper & Nicholsons.

Constructed of Canadian yellow pine on oak frames with teak trim and a lead keel, Ianthe retains around 80% of her original timber. She is the last surviving example of a once‑competitive Christchurch racing type, which comprised Ianthe, Iola, and Queen Bee.

Ianthe has spent all her life at Christchurch Sailing Club. A restoration by Rossiter Yachts (2002–03) renewed her keel, centreboard case and garboards. She has never had an engine.

There is an entry for Ianthe in the 1909 edition of Hunt’s Universal Yacht List, which was found at Cowes Library (entry number 1747). The entry was submitted in 1908 by Melvill Druitt, an ex commodore of Christchurch Sailing Club and owner of Ianthe​ between 1907 and 1947. He stated that she was built by Campers.

In 1992, her lines were taken off by Jim Mottram, a boat builder and member of Christchurch Sailing Club. Her long ownership under Melvill Druitt (1907–1947) and subsequently R. Whittingham (1947 to 1979) helped to ensure her survival.

In the summer, she is kept on a river mooring off Christchurch Sailing Club and has wintered in the same boatshed at the Club since 1913. She regularly attends the Yarmouth Old Gaffers Festival.

Today Ianthe is owned and maintained by an eight-member syndicate within Christchurch Sailing Club
